This role requires a strong blend of regional subject‑matter expertise, partner and sales enablement, and direct customer engagement, alongside hands‑on ownership of solution demonstrations and Proofs of Concept (PoCs). A successful candidate will be a trusted technical leader who collaborates closely with sales teams, channel partners, and customers to drive adoption and expansion of the Voca CIC portfolio across the region. They will also play a key role in shaping product direction by providing structured feedback to Product Management and Engineering teams, directly influencing the continued growth of AudioCodes’ Voca CIC presence across the region. About AudioCodes AudioCodes (Nasdaq: AUDC) is a global leader in enterprise voice technology and Voice AI innovation for the digital workplace and customer experience. We help organizations unlock the full value of voice, transforming every conversation into a strategic asset that drives smarter decisions, better experiences and business growth. Our portfolio spans secure voice infrastructure, unified communications and contact center, with next-generation AI-powered voice solutions. With over 30 years of expertise and presence in more than 100 countries, AudioCodes is trusted by 65 of the Fortune 100 to power intelligent, agile and future-ready interactions across businesses worldwide. Voca CIC: Award-winning AI-first CX for Microsoft Teams and more Voca CIC is AudioCodes' flagship, award-winning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) portfolio, designed to meet organizations where they are today and where they're going next. The portfolio covers two distinct opportunities: a Microsoft Teams-native contact center for organizations standardized on the Microsoft ecosystem, and a voice-platform-agnostic AI Receptionist that runs on top of any phone system. Voca CIC for Microsoft Teams is an AI-first, full omnichannel contact center, Microsoft Teams Unify certified and built natively in Azure on the same voice backbone that powers Microsoft Teams Phone. That delivers the tightest integration model on the market. Where other vendors "plug into" Teams through loose connectors, Voca CIC lives inside Teams, so every Teams user can play a role in the service workflow. It is AI-first by design, embedding Conversational AI and Generative AI into the agent and customer journey through AI voice agents, AI call summarization, and sentiment analysis, alongside an omnichannel toolkit that unifies voice, chat, and email into a single agent screen. Voca CIC has won three major industry awards in two years (CX Today Best Microsoft Teams Contact Center 2024, CX Today Best CX Deployment 2025, and UC Today Best Microsoft Teams Contact Center 2025), with more than 200 enterprise customers in production across 12+ Microsoft Azure regions worldwide. The Voca AI Receptionist is our standalone, entry-level AI offering for businesses of all sizes, from SMB to large enterprise. Built as a multi-platform solution that sits on top of any voice platform (Microsoft Teams, Cisco, Avaya, RingCentral, traditional PBX, or carrier voice services), it dramatically expands our addressable market well beyond the Microsoft footprint. It delivers AI-driven call routing, document and website-grounded Q&A, CRM integration, appointment scheduling, and outbound SMS to organizations looking for a fast on-ramp into AI-powered customer service, regardless of the phone system they already own. If you want to build at the intersection of Microsoft Teams, Azure, and applied AI, with real enterprises depending on your work every day, this is where it happens. Learn more about Voca CIC . Responsibilities We’re looking for an experienced Presales Engineer to lead and execute technical presales activities for Voca CIC across the APAC region. In this role, you’ll act as the regional subject‑matter expert, partnering closely with sales teams, channel partners, and customers to drive solution alignment and technical validation throughout the sales cycle. You’ll take hands‑on ownership of demos and Proofs of Concepts, enable partners through training and guidance, and collaborate cross‑functionally with Product and Engineering teams to bring market and customer insights back into the roadmap—helping translate innovation into measurable business growth. What You’ll Do 1) Regional SME Leadership Act as the APAC leading Technical Subject Matter Expert (SME) for AudioCodes Voca CIC Stay aligned with the product roadmap, releases, and feature enhancements Provide structured market, competitive, and customer feedback to product management and engineering teams Develop and maintain best practices, demo assets, and reusable solution playbooks Educate regional sales and pre‑sales teams through training sessions, enablement workshops, and product update briefings 2) Partner Engagement & Recruitment Support Support the recruitment and onboarding of new partners for Voca CIC across APAC through technical validation and capability assessments Enable partners through training programs, workshops, and hands-on technical sessions Act as a trusted technical advisor, helping partners design, build, and scale Voca CIC practices Collaborate closely with channel and alliance teams to identify, onboard, and grow strategic partners 3) Customer & Sales Engagement Deliver technical presentations, workshops, and solution walkthroughs to customers and prospects Support RFP and RFI responses with detailed technical architecture and solution input Partner with sales teams to drive pipeline progression, influence deal strategy, and close opportunities Position Voca CIC against competing platforms with clear technical and business differentiation 4) Demonstrations, PoCs & Demo Strategy Lead end-to

AudioCodes.description: Job Opportunities at AudioCodes - Explore Open Positions Home Careers Chief Information Officer (CIO) Description We are seeking an accomplished Chief Information Officer to join the Executive Leadership Team, report directly to the CEO , and lead the technology function across the company as a strategic partner to the business. The CIO will own our information technology strategy, run and continuously optimize our core enterprise systems, and champion the adoption of emerging technologies, with artificial intelligence at the center, to create measurable business value. The CIO will help shape the company's technology direction while enabling business growth, operational excellence, and innovation across the organization. Over the past three years the company completed a major transformation, replacing its legacy platform with a modern Oracle Fusion (Cloud ERP) environment that is now fully live and in steady-state operation. The incoming CIO will build on this foundation by keeping operational systems reliable and secure, extracting more value from the ERP investment, and leading the next wave of change. This includes a planned move to a new enterprise service management platform that will consolidate several of our current systems, along with the responsible integration of AI across the organization. Security is central to this role. Beyond our internal systems, we manage infrastructure on behalf of thousands of managed-services customers, so a strong security posture is essential to the business and to the trust our customers place in us. The CIO will own the overall security agenda, with the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) reporting into the role, and will be accountable for maintaining compliance with standards including SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR, while preparing the organization for FedRAMP in the near future. The ideal candidate pairs deep, hands-on technology expertise with strong business acumen. They understand that technology exists to run and grow the business, they are energized by the shift that AI is bringing to the IT world, and they are equally comfortable setting strategy, leading large programs, and getting into the detail of operational applications. This is an enterprise leadership role with broad influence across the company. AxonPulse.title: TECHNOLOGY
AxonPulse.description: Toggle High Contrast Toggle Font size Skip to content AI that turns complexity into clarity. PERCEPTION Perception at Axon Pulse detects targets early in noise and clutter, classifies them into reliable labels, and maintains continuous tracks through motion, occlusion, and sensor changes. Built for real-world conditions, it delivers low-latency, stable outputs with transparent reasoning for confident decision-making. DECISION & INTEGRATION Our in-house command and control delivers clear tracks, confidence, sensor evidence, and next-step guidance. It manages timing, audit, and failover, connects via clean APIs, and includes tools for analysis, training, and reporting. SUPER RESOLUTION Super resolution clarifies radar, acoustic, and signals data — recovering structure, separating sources, and estimating direction so operators see real targets. Physics-aware methods enhance detection, classification, and tracking without inventing features. SENSOR FUSION Sensor fusion delivers a single, trustworthy picture from diverse sensors and data streams. Our AI learns each source’s strengths and limits, fusing at measurement or track level as the mission demands. We align timing, handle dropouts, and adapt weights to reliability, geometry, and SNR. Cross-cueing requests the next best look. Consistency checks and deduplication keep one identity. Output: unified track and class with calibrated confidence and provenance. Behind Axon Pulse is a team of AI researchers and engineers with deep experience in radar, acoustics, optics, and intelligence systems.

AutoFleet.description: AI for Fleets: A Complete Guide to Fleet Management AI Tools Book your demo Book Your Demo We use cookies on our website to see how you interact with it. Privacy Policy Accept All Blog AI for Fleets: The industry’s guide for making AI work for your fleet Sima Megrel Shubzak , VP of Marketing October 30, 2025 Key Insights Let’s put all the buzzwords aside for a moment. In essence, AI for fleets is about using digital tools to get a better understanding of what is happening in the fleet, making better decisions, and taking action faster. This blog is the summary of our series on AI for fleets. The series was written as part of our ongoing commitment to help fleet managers, maintenance supervisors, fleet analysts, coordinators and dispatchers, route planners, safety officers, procurement specialists, and other fleet professionals understand what AI tools are currently available for fleets and help make informed decisions on how to work AI into your fleet management and operations stack. So far, the series includes: ‍ AI for Field Service Routing ‍ AI for Fleet Management Optimization AI for Last-Mile Delivery with more to come. AI works by incorporating and processing data from numerous sources. Using this data, an AI engine can produce unprecedented visibility, both real-time and historical, launch automated workflows as necessary, and provide the tools, insights, and even recommendations to improve fleet performance easily. At its best, AI learns what works for your fleet or service and implements it continuously, cutting down costs and staffing, and providing a clear view into your operation. The Daily Fleet Reality: Too Many Systems, Not Enough Truth The reality of many fleets and transportation systems is that of multiple separate systems operating independently. Data is scattered across TMS, CMMS, and email, as well as telematics and fleet management systems. Dispatchers and planners typically learn about delays too late to fix them, safety teams can drown in dashcam footage, and fleet managers face mounting costs. Technology made fleet operations more efficient, but it created new challenges. Teams spend their days firefighting and flipping between screens instead of planning and taking care of the fleet. That is where AI comes in, organizing data, collecting information across systems, and creating a unified single pane of glass. Moreover, using AI goes beyond efficiency and time management. It allows decisions to be made based on insights grounded in facts, not just gut feelings, and provides access to analytics and facts that can be nearly impossible to access otherwise. Bringing Everything Together: One Source of Truth So the first challenge AI can help with is making your existing systems talk to each other properly and present you with a clear, unified picture of the state of your fleet. The goal is simple: create one operational picture that everyone can trust and act on. When the fleet manager, the driver, the route planner, and the technician all look at the same task, they should see the same ETA, the same status, the same plan. No more separate systems, each showing a fraction of the information. Connecting your fragmented data streams—GPS positions, vehicle status, work orders, inventory levels, traffic conditions, and more—requires the AI engine to synchronize, harmonize, normalize, and standardize data and translate it into a common language. Visibility matters, and without it, you cannot make informed decisions. Optimizing Fleets for Reality: Balancing What Actually Matters Here are some examples of how AI earns its keep: ensuring SLA compliance even when a vehicle needs servicing, optimizing charging to stay within energy budgets, monitoring driver safety without requiring extensive in-cab footage review, and there are many more. An effective AI for fleets doesn't make decisions for you—it helps you make them better and faster. You tell the system what matters to your business: examples include on-time performance, cost per stop, driver workload, vehicle maintenance, emissions, safety, etc. The system finds plans that balance these priorities the way you want, not the way some algorithm thinks is optimal. More importantly, it can adjust those priorities on the fly, for example: Some examples of AI powered dynamic optimizations Your operations team controls these dials, not your IT department. Automating Fleet Management Tasks: Where AI Handles the Routine AI dashboards show you what's happening. An automation engine makes things happen smoothly with your guidance. Once you have reliable data and smart optimization, you can start connecting insights directly to actions. This can help take the load off of your fleet management team, handling most routine cases automatically and leaving your people to handle exceptions, plan, and strategize. Think about the patterns fleet teams handle every single day: Vehicle malfunction. Your telematics reports that a warning light has just turned on in one of your vehicles. An alert on your dashboard automatically triggers an AI agent that creates the relevant work order. If the maintenance model indicates that the issue is not critical, it schedules the work during off-peak hours, identifies a replacement vehicle, and alerts the supervisor. If it is urgent, it reroutes the driver to an available workshop and replans the day across the fleet, relocating tasks as necessary. Urgent request from a VIP client. An AI agent checks all current plans and finds the best fit. Your dispatcher then reviews the plan, approves it with one click, and moves on, while the AI recalculates everyone's day, messages the right driver with instructions, and updates the customer with a realistic ETA. An electric vehicle needs to be charged. Automations can take care of even the most day-to-day fleet tasks, like charging EV vehicles. The AI continually monitors the fleet and looks ahead using your CRM or ERP

Privacy Policy Accept All eGuides State of Autonomous Vehicles: 2025’s AV Push Toward a Driverless Future Sima Megrel Shubzak , VP of Marketing April 14, 2025 Key Insights The world of autonomous mobility isn't just evolving—it's accelerating at breakneck speed. From San Francisco to Shanghai, driverless cars can now be seen navigating traffic, and robotaxis and autonomous shuttles are becoming more common. 2025 is shaping up to become a watershed year for the autonomous vehicle industry as new launches and expansions are being announced. This transportation revolution is backed by tech giants and automotive innovators like Google’s Waymo, Amazon’s Zoox, Uber, Tesla, Alibaba, and Baidu, with strategic partnerships, cutting-edge technology, and billions spent on perfecting systems that can outperform human drivers. As psychological barriers crumble and regulatory frameworks adapt to promising safety data, we stand at the threshold of a fundamental shift in how humanity moves. Who is leading the charge? What’s next for the industry? Let’s dive in: ‍ Autonomous transporation availabilty around the world Robotaxi expansion - Waymo's and Uber tie-in Waymo, a subsidiary of Google’s Alphabet, has been at the forefront of autonomous mobility in the US for a while now. In late 2024, Waymo expanded its autonomous taxi partnership with Uber to include Austin and Atlanta, building upon their initial collaboration in Phoenix. This partnership allows these two leaders in shared mobility to play to each other’s strengths, allowing Uber users to hail Waymo's autonomous vehicles directly through the Uber app, enhancing accessibility to self-driving technology. In this collaboration, Waymo provides the driverless cars and handles roadside assistance and customer service, while Uber brings in the customers. Uber is leveraging its huge install base to future-proof and actively expand its presence in autonomous mobility, weaving a web of partnerships in the field. Recent announcements include WeRide in Abu Dhabi launched in December 2024 (with a human safety driver); and Wayve out of the UK, as well as a collaboration with May Mobility and Chinese startup Momenta. Uber is also collaborating with Avride to introduce autonomous delivery robots in cities like Dallas and Austin. One partnership not in the stars , at least for now, is between Uber and Tesla, who prefers to go at it alone. Tesla and Amazon’s Zoox are betting on themselves, and building their own autonomous services Tesla announced very ambitious plans for autonomous mobility. In October 2024, it unveiled the Cybercab, a two-seater robotaxi designed for urban transportation. Tesla has its own distinct vision for an autonomous car, relying on software and a much cheaper, camera-only, sensor array, backed by the vast data it has from all its vehicles already on the road. Data used to train its AI driver. Tesla believes it can go toe-to-toe with their sensor-heavy competitors. But so far, Tesla has only been successful in reaching level 3 autonomy, allowing drivers to take their hands off the wheel and letting the car drive itself, but still requiring a driver. This presents a great test case for the industry: comparing two approaches and seeing which one will prevail—Tesla's big fleet without geographical limitations versus Waymo's sensor-heavy, smaller, and geo-fenced fleet that is already offering Level 4 autonomy commercially. Tesla plans to launch robotaxis as early as June 2025 in Austin, Texas . Two approaches to achieve widespread autonomous mobility Lyft is also making strides in the autonomous mobility arena through strategic partnerships. Collaborating with May Mobility, Lyft plans to deploy autonomous Toyota Sienna minivans in Atlanta by the end of 2025, with subsequent expansions to Dallas by 2026. Additionally, Lyft is making strides towards introducing its own robotaxi together with with Mobileye and Marubeni aiming to launch in Dallas and scale to other cities in 2026. Lastly, Zoox, the Amazon subsidiary, has made notable strides in autonomous mobility by developing its purpose-built robotaxi with no traditional controls like a steering wheel. Zoox plans to launch the service in Las Vegas and the San Francisco Bay Area in 2025. Zoox recently had to face some difficulty with its autonomous vehicle, resulting in a software recall due to unexpected braking, whose impact on its launch schedule remains to be seen. Autonomous transportation value chain, and the position of some of the key players in the industry Autonomous Mobility in Europe and China China has some of the leading autonomous vehicle services in the world. It is backed by the Chinese government and by national guidelines that provide clear standards for testing, production, and commercial deployment of autonomous vehicles. Baidu's Apollo Go, Alibaba’s AutoX, SAIC Motors, and US-Chinese partnerships like WeRide and Pony.ai have all committed to deploying large numbers of autonomous vehicles in 2025, with Apollo eyeing international markets too. In Europe, the autonomous vehicle (AV) landscape takes on a different character, and it is focused on public transport-like, route-centric AVs, such as roboshuttles, robovans, and robobuses. These vehicles are currently primarily deployed in testing sites for short, low-usage trips, often serving underserved areas. Interestingly, Europe is the first to implement multiple autonomous vehicle providers on the same service, breaking silos and providing a unified service. Mobility giant Keolis has had experience operating such a service, using Autofleet to manage a multi-provider AV fleet. But autonomous mobility using cars is not unheard of in Europe, and some providers are already testing robocars there, alongside services bei

Do you want to use your scientific credibility and business acumen to shape treatment pathways and inform brand strategy while staying close to the evidence? As an MSL at AstraZeneca, you will build trusted scientific partnerships with Key External Experts and healthcare professionals, translating the latest data into meaningful insights and actions. You will be 60% field-based, engaging face-to-face across your territory and partnering closely with an office-based Medical Affairs Manager for your therapeutic area to connect scientific strategy with on-the-ground reality. In this role, you will help align medical and commercial objectives without compromising on ethics—fueling our growth and enabling continued investment in research. Your work will ensure that the right data reaches the right stakeholders at the right time, improving decision-making and, ultimately, patient outcomes. Accountabilities: Scientific Exchange and Insight Generation: Conduct high-quality scientific discussions with KEEs and HCPs; gather and synthesize field insights to inform medical strategy and brand planning.Therapeutic Area Mastery: Maintain up-to-date expertise on the TA, treatment paradigms, and competitor data through literature review, congress attendance, and expert engagement.Account Plan Execution: Deliver medical components of account plans to time and budget, ensuring activities address identified gaps and opportunities.Expert Partnership Development: Build deep, trust-based relationships with KEEs; map interests, identify collaboration opportunities, and support local practice change.Evidence Discussion and Data Gap Identification: Present and discuss key data sets to uncover evidence gaps, patient pathways, and unmet needs aligned to TA strategy.Scientific Events and Education: Initiate and co-create scientific events with KEEs; lead journal clubs and one-to-one scientific exchanges that elevate disease and therapy understanding.Digital Medical Engagement: Produce compliant scientific digital content (e.g., newsletters, approved emails) as part of integrated medical plans to broaden reach and impact.Field Intelligence and Internal Collaboration: Share actionable insights with cross-functional teams; contribute to the core strategic plan and educate key account managers and colleagues on disease and therapies.Clinical Study and Early Access Support: Support AZ-sponsored clinical studies (site selection and initiation) and contribute to bridging/early access programs where relevant.Externally Sponsored Research and Funding Stewardship: Manage ESRs, grants, donations, and third-party scientific sponsorships with rigor and transparency.Real-World Evidence and Care Transformation: Identify partners, including KEEs and Sick Funds, to develop real-world data initiatives and care-improvement projects that enable local practice change.Network and Best Practice Sharing: Collaborate with MSLs across countries and TAs to exchange best practices and continuously evolve the role.Congress Participation: Attend national congresses and, as required, represent the TA at international meetings to bring back insights and strengthen external networks.Medical Information and Documentation: Respond to medical information requests via approved platforms; document all interactions thoroughly and on time in the designated systems.Compliance and Continuous Improvement: Complete all training; uphold AZ policies and external codes; seek feedback through training and joint field visits to refine communication and insight-gathering skills. Essential Skills/Experience: - MD/PharmD/PhD/DVM or equivalent - Significant and robust experience with searching, handling, assimilating, synthesizing, reporting, and presenting scientific data in the healthcare sector- Quick self-learner, ability, and willingness to work in a team and independently.- National mobility and flexibility in attendance of local events outside of working hours- Ability to multitask effectively, demonstrate strong time management skills, and excel under pre-specified deadlines- Excellent relational and communication skills- Ability to build and maintain strategic partnerships with a diverse range of stakeholders.- Takes initiative and proactive were needed while conscious of compliance and process rules in the company- Presentation skills- Medical integrity and ethical balance- Fluent knowledge of English (verbal and written) Desirable Skills/Experience: - Experience in and knowledge of pharmaceutical medical and marketing processes- Knowledge of therapeutic area. Broad employability in other TAs is an asset.- Experience in moderation of meetings with HCPs- Business Acumen- Proven Project management skills- Digital capabilities, experience in creating digital assets- Ability to rapidly shift between multiple projects and managing field-office workload - Experience in production of scientific events- Ability to distinguish between the main and the minor Why AstraZeneca: Here, science and strategy meet to accelerate impact for patients. You will join a team that brings medical experts, commercial thinkers, and innovators into the same room to unlock bold ideas—always guided by evidence and strong ethics. We move with agility, learn fast from what works and what doesn’t, and stay close to a broad, science-led pipeline that keeps our work varied and meaningful. Your insights from the field will shape decisions across the business, helping us invest wisely in research while improving how patients are diagnosed, treated, and cared for. AstraZeneca.description: Lung Cancer Specialist-Center-North at AstraZeneca Skip to main content Oncology Sales Search jobs Lung Cancer Specialist-Center-North Location Kfar Saba, Central District, Israel Job ID R-258544 Date posted 05/09/2026 Apply Job Title: Lung Cancer Specialist-Center-North Introduction to role Are you ready to change the trajectory of lung cancer by turning cutting-edge science into real-world impact? Do you thrive in a fast-moving environment where bold ideas and crisp execution accelerate better outcomes for patients and the business? In this field-based role, you will lead the commercial strategy and execution for our lung cancer portfolio across the Center-North territory, translating brand priorities into measurable results. You will uncover opportunities across the patient journey, remove barriers to optimal care, and ensure that the right patients receive the right medicine at the right time. Working closely with cross-functional partners, you will bring clarity, urgency and precision to a complex market. This position is designed for impact from day one. Expect four days per week in the field building relationships and driving performance, and one day focused on planning, learning and project work. Your ownership of the territory will help shape care pathways and fuel launches that redefine standards of care. Accountabilities - Sales Excellence and Territory Leadership: Achieve or exceed lung cancer portfolio targets by building and executing a territory plan aligned to brand and therapy-area priorities. Focus resources where they will create the greatest clinical and commercial impact and manage budgets for maximum return.- Insight-Driven Execution: Use sales, market and customer data to map the patient journey, quantify gaps and risks, and set clear priorities. Continuously adapt plans to changes in competition, guidelines and local treatment dynamics to sustain momentum.- Customer Engagement and Omnichannel Impact: Build trusted, long-term relationships with oncologists and wider care teams. Deliver relevant, personalized engagements across face-to-face, digital and omnichannel channels. Lead or support customer initiatives that address bottlenecks in diagnosis, testing and treatment, and feed insights into territory and cross-functional planning.- Oncology Knowledge and Cross-Functional Collaboration: Maintain deep understanding of disease biology, treatment pathways, our medicines and the competitive landscape. Communicate approved scientific and product information clearly. Partner with Brand, Medical, Market Access and Diagnostics to align opportunities and execute launches and strategic initiatives with excellence.- Compliance and Professional Standards: Conduct all activities in line with AstraZeneca’s Code of Ethics, policies, local regulations and industry standards. Uphold integrity, transparency and professionalism in every interaction.- Immediate to Long-Term Impact: In your first 90 days, establish a sharp territory plan, map priority accounts and secure early wins. Over time, shape pathway adoption, enable successful indications and launches, and contribute to repeatable commercial excellence across the portfolio. Essential Skills/Experience - Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, healthcare, business or a related field.- Proven experience in pharmaceutical or specialty-care sales.- Demonstrated success in achieving sales and business objectives.- Strong communication, influencing, negotiation and presentation skills.- Strong relationship-building and stakeholder-management capabilities.- Ability to interpret data and translate insights into actions.- Ability to manage a complex territory independently and work effectively in a cross-functional environment.- Proficiency with CRM systems, digital tools and data-driven decision-making. Desirable Skills/Experience - Previous oncology or specialty-care experience.- Understanding of cancer care pathways and treatment guidelines.- Experience launching new products or indications in a competitive market.- Experience in strategic account management.- Omnichannel customer-engagement experience. Why AstraZeneca Join a team where science and enterprise move in lockstep to deliver transformative medicines to people living with cancer. You will operate at pace, trusted to make smart, data-grounded decisions and encouraged to challenge convention when it accelerates patient impact. Expect unexpected teams in the same room—medical experts, data minds and commercial leaders—co-creating solutions and acting quickly. Our pipeline is deep and advancing fast, creating meaningful opportunities to lead launches, shape care environments and see the results of your work in clinics. We value kindness alongside ambition, empowering you to take ownership, speak up and grow as you deliver for patients. Call to Action If you are ready to turn bold science into better outcomes for people with lung cancer across the Center-North territory, step forward and apply to shape what comes next! We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse team representing all backgrounds, with as wide a range of perspectives as possible, and harnessing industry-leading skills. We believe that the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We welcome and consider applications to join our team from all qualified candidates, regardless of their characteristics. We comply with all applicable laws and regulations on non-discrimination in employment (and recruitment), as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements. Beach Bum.title: About Us
Beach Bum.description: About Us Our Story Over the years, Beach Bum has grown into a global success story with hit titles like Lord of the Board, Spades Royale, Gin Rummy Stars, Domino Go, Rummy Rush, OPA!, and more to come! The company brings countless hours of joy to millions of loyal players around the world. In 2021, Beach Bum was acquired by Voodoo, a global tech company that entertains the world through iconic apps and games. Voodoo was founded in 2013 and became well‑known for publishing highly popular free‑to‑play mobile games, such as Mob Control, Paper.io 2, and Hole.io, and many others, with billions of total downloads worldwide. Since its founding, Voodoo has expanded beyond hyper‑casual titles to include a wide range of casual and hybrid games, and has worked with thousands of external studios to bring new games to market. The acquisition of Beach Bum was part of Voodoo’s strategy to diversify its portfolio and strengthen its presence in the casual gaming space, combining Voodoo’s expertise in game growth and monetization with Beach Bum’s deep experience in in‑app purchases and mobile adaptations of classic games. Together, Beach Bum and Voodoo continue to delight players around the globe with engaging and social gaming experiences. Leadership Yuval Dor CEO Yuval is a gaming industry veteran with over 20 years of experience, including senior leadership positions at companies such as Playtika and Moon Active. Having grown up in the analytics domain, Yuval is passionate about finding the true value behind every action. He is a big believer in people and their ability to make a great impact on the company in many different ways. Outside of the gaming world, Yuval is a proud dad to three children and one Hila Shachar CFO With over 20 years of financial leadership, Hila’s background includes executive roles such as CFO at Nielsen Innovate and Senior Manager at Ernst & Young. With a career built at the intersection of the startup ecosystem and the venture capital world, Hila focuses on finding the strategic value behind the numbers to drive growth. She knows that in any venture, the most important investment is always in the people who make it happen. Outside of the financial world, Hila is a passionate foodie who loves exploring the fine dining scene and discovering new culinary experiences. Shiri Livne GM, Backgammon Shiri is a gaming industry leader with extensive experience in monetization and growth strategy across some of the world’s leading social card and board games. After leading Spades Royale and Domino Go as GM, Shiri now manages Beach Bum’s flagship Backgammon game, focusing on growth, innovation, and building high-performing teams. Known for her fast-paced mindset and hands-on leadership style, Shiri is passionate about creating player experiences people truly love. Outside of gaming, she’s a surfer, sports enthusiast, and adrenaline seeker who thrives on challenges, high energy, and pushing boundaries. Yair Yehezkel GM, Portfolio Yair Yehezkel has over a decade of product expertise across multiple industries. At Beach Bum, Yair has driven the release of multiple titles, such as OPA! and Rummy Rush. With a background in game design, Yair leads game innovation through creative and technical strategies designed for large-scale impact. Omri Ohayon VP R&D Omri is a technology leader with 15 years in the gaming industry, bringing an end-to-end perspective on how games and their infrastructure get built. He has hands-on experience across nearly every domain of game development and operations — from player-facing systems to backend infrastructure. A passionate AI advocate, Omri championed the adoption of generative AI tools like Claude Code across BeachBum’s engineering. Omri holds a degree in Software Engineering. Biobeat.title: About Us
Biobeat.description: WELCOME TO BIOBEAT Transforming Healthcare Through Innovation Biobeat is revolutionizing care with its groundbreaking advancements in diagnosis and management of hypertension. Our cuff-less, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring system enhances clinical decision-making and optimizes patient care by eliminating the stress and inconvenience of traditional methods Who We Are We are a team of passionate individuals driven by a shared mission to make a positive impact on healthcare. From engineers and data scientists to healthcare professionals and industry experts, our diverse team brings together a wealth of knowledge and experience to drive innovation and change in the healthcare landscape. Our Mission Our mission is simple yet ambitious: To ensure all hypertension patients are monitored and managed effectively. Driving Change in Healthcare Traditional healthcare practices often face challenges in accurately diagnosing and treating patients. Biobeat is on a mission to provide complete and accurate information to allow physicians to make informed decisions for their patients. Through our FDA-cleared blood pressure monitoring system, we aim to tackle misdiagnosis and provide support for optimal treatment Our Approach At Biobeat, we leverage the latest advancements in wearable technology and data analytics to develop innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of healthcare providers and patients. Our comprehensive monitoring platform enables tracking of vital signs, allowing a physician to make informed decisions, of health issues and personalized interventions. Biobeat's Solution With Biobeat’s proprietary patented PPG sensor for capturing accurate measurements, our blood pressure monitoring solution is designed to simplify and enhance the management of hypertension. We focus on providing physicians with precise insights into their patients’ health. Our approach ensures continuous monitoring, enabling timely interventions and personalized care plans. Our Values Innovation We foster a culture of innovation, constantly pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in healthcare technology. Integrity We operate with honesty, transparency, and ethical integrity in all aspects of our business. We have regulatory approvals and certificates in USA, Europe and many other places. Collaboration We believe in the power of collaboration, in unmasking the silent killer, working closely with healthcare providers, researchers, and industry partners to drive positive change. Excellence We strive for excellence in everything we do, from product development to customer support, to deliver the highest quality solutions and services. Patient focus We are committed to delivering a reliable blood pressure monitoring solution that empower physicians to manage their patients’ hypertension with ease and confidence. Our goal is to offer continuous, accurate, and convenient healthcare monitoring, enabling proactive management and improved patient outcomes. Join Us in Shaping the Future of Healthcare At Biobeat, we believe that collaboration is key to driving meaningful change in healthcare. Whether you’re a healthcare provider, researcher, or technology enthusiast, we invite you to join us on our journey to transform healthcare delivery and improve patient outcomes. In this role, you will be the primary owner of the customer relationship from the moment a deal closes through the full lifecycle of the account. This is not a passive account management role; it is a deeply operational, field-oriented position where you will translate the BiltOn platform into measurable operational value for construction clients. You will drive onboarding, ensure platform adoption, manage complex stakeholder relationships, and serve as the expert voice of the customer within BiltOn. Key Responsibilities: End-to-End Account Ownership: Act as the primary relationship owner for a portfolio of construction accounts. Adoption & Value Realization: Proactively monitor usage dashboards, identify at-risk accounts, and execute recovery plans to ensure customers derive maximum ROI from our platform. Field Engagement: Conduct site visits to observe operations, reinforce product usage, train site officials/foremen, and identify operational pain points that BiltOn can solve. Integration Coordination: Lead customer-facing integrations (e.g., Procore, Autodesk Build) from kickoff to execution. Train site teams on integrated workflows and troubleshoot sync issues in partnership with Product and Engineering. Strategic Reviews: Partner with Account Executives to deliver Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) with executive stakeholders, presenting adoption data, compliance trends, and roadmap alignment. Cross-Functional Advocacy: Capture and translate structured product feedback and feature requests into business impact, advocating for customer requirements with our Product and Engineering teams. Escalation Management: Own customer-facing communication during incidents or unresolved issues, coordinating internally until resolution. Qualifications: Experience: 3–5 years of experience in Customer Success or Account Management, preferably in SaaS, construction-tech, or field operations environments. Operational Mindset: Demonstrated ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder workflows and operational processes. You are comfortable balancing office-based strategy with "boots on the ground" field work. Communication Skills: Exceptional interpersonal skills. You can speak the language of construction foremen, superintendents, and project executives with equal credibility. Technical Proficiency: Ability to quickly master new software systems (CRM/Salesforce, Jira, Slack) and understand integrations (Procore/Autodesk knowledge is a significant plus). Data-Driven: Proficiency in tracking and analyzing usage metrics to identify trends, mitigate churn, and drive growth. Problem Solver: Proven track record of managing escalations and finding creative solutions to site-specific challenges. Field Readiness: Willingness and ability to perform site visits and represent BiltOn in the field. Why Join BiltOn: You will join a high-growth, mission-driven organization that is digitizing the construction industry. Axonius.description: Axonius Correlated Partner Program Earns Fourth Consecutive 5-Star Rating | Axonius Webinar: Sept 22 | Back to Basics: AI Security that Actually Works Register Now Axonius Correlated Partner Program Continues Momentum with Fourth Consecutive 5-Star Rating in CRN® Partner Program May 1, 2024 Axonius Correlated Partner Program earns fourth consecutive 5-star rating in CRN Partner Program Guide, showcasing exponential growth and expansion opportunities for partners in cybersecurity asset management. Recognition follows record breaking year of channel ARR growth NEW YORK, NY — May 1, 2024 — Axonius , the leader in cybersecurity asset management and SaaS management , today announced the Axonius Correlated Partner Program has been recognized for the fourth consecutive year by CRN® , a brand of The Channel Company , with a prestigious 5-star rating in its 2024 Partner Program Guide. The program has been continuously recognized for its commitment to delivering profitable, successful, and secure channel partnerships worldwide — a testament to the consistency and stability of the Axonius core channel offerings as a service provider. This year, the Axonius Correlated Partner Program expanded its capabilities and launched offerings in new markets to better serve the needs of its partners. These updates include: New enablement journeys through the newly-developed Axonius 6.0 as the system of record for their clients’ digital infrastructure EMEA channel growth with strategic team hires in the region Most impactfully, Axonius Correlated Partner Program has formally launched the Axonius Managed Service Program , designed to empower Axonius Partners to scale their channel business to new heights, generate new revenue routes, and drive efficiency. The new program represents how Axonius has long met the ongoing challenge to build with their partners, especially for MSPs. “Our Axonius Correlated Partner Program and channel ecosystem has experienced tremendous growth in the last year and we understand it's important to continue to evolve and add additional growth opportunities for our partners,” said Mark Daggett, Vice President of Worldwide Channels and Alliances at Axonius. “As part of that evolution this year, we're extremely excited about entering into the Managed Services Market with our partner community. This expansion, coupled with our geographic growth in Southern Europe and other parts of the continent, solidifies our commitment to meeting our partners’ needs worldwide.” The Axonius Correlated Partner Program witnessed unprecedented growth this year as one of the best-in-class partner programs in the channel ecosystem. The Channel Business saw 76% Growth YoY in ARR from 2022 to 2023, with 95% of the total company ARR connected to the channel, up from 80% in 2022. A third of its overall channel business was Partner Initiated, making partnerships a crucial aspect of overall business performance. Axonius itself had one of its most impressive years yet, achieving $100M ARR in 2023 and most recently securing $200M in a Series E extension round. “The unprecedented pace of technological growth and offerings demands a partner who understands the needs of the channel,” said Dustin Patterson, Senior Director of Cyber Security Managed Services at ConvergeOne. “Vendors and service providers that can provide trust, secure services, and adaptability to the ever-changing market are critical. I’m proud to see Axonius recognized again in CRN’s 2024 Channel Program Guide, knowing that their unfettered commitment to delivering excellent service to the IT channel has made undeniable impacts across their partnerships in the industry.” In addition to receiving a fourth consecutive 5-star rating this year, Axonius Vice President of Worldwide Channels and Alliances Mark Daggett was named to the 2024 CRN® Channel Chiefs list for the fourth consecutive year, and Axonius again made CRN’s 2024 Security List 100 . The 2024 Partner Program Guide will be featured in the April 2024 issue of CRN and online . To learn more about the Axonius Correlated Partner Program, visit the website . By providing insight into the bigger picture of how every asset is managed and secured, partners can drive more strategic conversations with customers — becoming trusted advisors for long-term success. Learn more at https://www.axonius.com/partners . To learn more about the Axonius Platform, take a product tour or request a demo . Axonius.description: The 20 Coolest Security Operations, Risk And Threat Intelligence Of 2024: The Security 100 The 20 Coolest Security Operations, Risk And Threat Intelligence Of 2024: The Security 100 From vendors that provide modern SIEM to those offering advanced threat feeds, here’s a look at 20 key companies in security operations, risk and threat intelligence. The arrival of generative AI marks another turning point in the security operations market, with many vendors now offering GenAI-powered tools that aim to dramatically boost productivity and effectiveness for Security Operations Center (SOC) teams. [Related: 10 Cybersecurity Companies Making Moves: January 2024 ] Many teams are now looking to leverage GenAI tools in tandem with their SIEM (security information and event management) and SOAR (security orchestration, automation and response) systems, in an effort to expedite their response times and improve their security decision-making. The SIEM space itself, meanwhile, continues to be highly competitive. The most recent Gartner Magic Quadrant for SIEM (from late 2022) ranks Microsoft, Splunk, IBM, Securonix and Exabeam in the “leaders” quadrant. In the realm of threat intelligence, top providers include Google Cloud (through its Mandiant subsidiary) and Recorded Future, while major players in risk management include Tenable and Qualys. What follows are the 20 security operations, risk and threat intelligence companies that made our Security 100 for 2024. Arctic Wolf Nick Schneider President, CEO Arctic Wolf launched a retainer option for its cyber incident response services, which aims to allow partners to more easily supply customers with rapid access to the services. The Arctic Wolf Incident Response JumpStart Retainer features a guarantee that cyber incidents will receive a response within one hour, backed by a service-level agreement. Axonius Dean Sysman Co-Founder, CEO Axonius unveiled a major new update to its platform that seeks to provide comprehensive visibility into installed software applications. With the introduction of software management as an addon capability, the Axonius platform can now consume inventories of installed software. BlueVoyant Jim Rosenthal Co-Founder, CEO With the acquisition of Conquest Cyber, BlueVoyant gains a company specializing in providing cloud security to Microsoft customers in the government sector. BlueVoyant said the deal provides robust cybersecurity assessment and compliance capabilities with an enhanced ability to identify gaps in customers’ security posture. Cribl Clint Sharp Co-Founder, CEO Cribl offers a data platform whose mission is to enable improved flexibility and control around security and IT data. The company aims to serve as an agnostic data engine, with the ability to route data—including from Splunk—and then place that data into a data lake or take other security-focused actions with it. Devo Technology Walter Scott CEO Devo has introduced a new threat intelligence feed inside its Devo Collective Defense security data platform that aims to enable enhanced defense against emerging cyberthreats. Other moves have included the launch of Devo DeepTrace, an AI-powered alert investigation tool that can build “complete” traces of suspicious activity within an organization’s IT infrastructure. Exabeam Adam Geller CEO Exabeam’s major recent product included Outcomes Navigator, which brings improved visualization to the company’s New-Scale SIEM platform. The offering provides a look into the security of current configurations in an environment and provides detailed recommendations for making improvements. Google Cloud Thomas Kurian CEO Google Cloud’s new Security AI Workbench offering is powered by a security-specific large language model known as SecPaLM. The model utilizes Google Cloud’s security intelligence via Google’s broad visibility into threat data and Mandiant ’s threat intel around vulnerabilities and malware. IBM Security Arvind Krishna Chairman, CEO IBM debuted its IBM Security QRadar Suite For Analysts, which is SaaS-delivered and includes re-architected threat detection and response offerings to improve speed and efficiency. Upgrades include a unified experience, simplified deployment through SaaS delivery and over 900 integrations with third-party tools. Infima Cybersecurity Joel Cahill Co-Founder, CEO The provider of highly automated security awareness training is focused on meeting the needs of MSPs. Infima said that its next-gen security awareness training platform provides dramatically simplified administration for MSPs, including speedy setup and minimal oversight once it’s up and running. KnowBe4 Stu Sjouwerman Founder, CEO KnowBe4, which provides security awareness training as well as security tools including anti-phishing, has expanded its portfolio with new tools including its QR Code Phishing Security Test offering. The tool aims to help organizations with identifying which of their users are most likely to be susceptible to malicious QR code threats. Qualys Sumedh Thakar President, CEO Qualys unveiled a major update to its risk management platform with the option for application security teams to bring detections of their own to use on the platform. AppSec teams will be able to bring detection and remediation scripts as Qualys IDs to the company’s vulnerability management, detection and response platform. Rapid7 Corey Thomas CEO Recent product updates from Rapid7 have included the addition of cloud anomaly detection utilizing AI-based, agentless capabilities. Rapid7 said the offering leverages its proprietary AI engine to detect suspicious behavior, which can then prompt automatic adjustments of configurations and privileges using the Rapid7 platform. Recorded Future Christopher Ahlberg Co-Founder, CEO Recorded Future enhanced its Intelligence Cloud platform, which is aimed at providing better visibility into threats and more automation of processes. Axonius.description: Axonius Is Named To The 2024 Forbes Cloud 100 | Axonius Webinar: Sept 22 | Back to Basics: AI Security that Actually Works Register Now Axonius Is Named To The 2024 Forbes Cloud 100 Aug 6, 2024 Axonius secures its spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 list for the fourth consecutive year, showcasing its growth, innovation, and commitment to customer success in the cloud industry. The company’s continued growth and commitments to innovation and customer success lead to its fourth consecutive feature on the list SAN FRANCISCO (August 6, 2024) – Axonius has been named to the Forbes 2024 Cloud 100, the definitive ranking of the top 100 private cloud companies in the world, published by Forbes in partnership with Bessemer Venture Partners and Salesforce Ventures . “It is a great honor to be named to the Forbes Cloud 100 yet again,” said Dean Sysman, CEO and Co-Founder of Axonius. “After a year of rapid growth and key milestones for our company, one thing never changes: our commitment to supporting our customers’ most complex security and IT challenges. Earning this recognition for the fourth straight year is a testament to this commitment being the core of our business, and to the hard work of our team.” In March 2024, Axonius announced it secured $200 million in a Series E extension funding round. The company also shared it had crossed the highly-coveted $100 million ARR milestone . In late 2023, Axonius released Axonius 6.0, a unified platform that provides a comprehensive understanding of all assets, their relationships, and business-level context. Axonius is now the only company to offer a combined solution for Cyber Asset Attack Surface Management (CAASM), SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM), and SaaS Management Platforms (SMP). What’s more, Axonius offers over 1,000 platform integrations, the most of any company in the space. This means that Axonius can surface more information than any other about security gaps, risk, misconfigurations, cost inefficiencies, and more. “IT and security teams at over 600 hundred organizations across the globe are using the Axonius Platform to manage an always-expanding sprawl of devices, users, software, SaaS applications, cloud services, and more. We provide a system of record for all their digital infrastructure so they can quickly mitigate threats, navigate risk, automate action, and inform business-level strategy. Customers love Axonius and have given us the highest net promoter score known by any cybersecurity or IT vendor in history,” said Sysman. For the ninth consecutive year, the Cloud 100 reviews submissions from hundreds of cloud startups and private companies each year. The Cloud 100 evaluation process involved ranking companies across four factors: market leadership (35%), estimated valuation (30%), operating metrics (20%), and people & culture (15%). For market leadership, the Cloud 100 enlists the help of a judging panel of public cloud company CEOs who assist in evaluating and ranking their private company peers. “Across nine years of data, we have yet to see as competitive of a cohort as the 2024 Cloud 100. The list value reached $820 billion this year, the highest list value in Cloud 100 history,” said Mary D’Onofrio, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners. "The Cloud 100 list represents the best of the best, and we've never been more excited about what the future holds, not only for the cloud but for the entire technology industry. We are proud of what these founders and their communities have already accomplished, and look forward to seeing how they continue to transform the industry in the future," said Paul Drews, managing partner at Salesforce Ventures. Axonius.title: CRN Security 100
Axonius.description: The 20 Coolest Security Operations, Risk And Threat Intelligence Of 2025: The Security 100 The 20 Coolest Security Operations, Risk And Threat Intelligence Of 2025: The Security 100 From vendors that provide modern SIEM to those offering advanced threat feeds, here’s a look at 20 key companies in security operations, risk and threat intelligence. When it comes to the crucial work of security operations teams, GenAI has rapidly made inroads — with countless tools now offering capabilities that can simplify and expedite the work of security analysts in responding to threats. Security analysts are now utilizing GenAI capabilities in a major way along with their SIEM (security information and event management) and SOAR (security orchestration, automation and response) tools, as a way to accelerate their responses and improve their security outcomes. [Related: 10 Major Ransomware Attacks And Data Breaches In 2024 ] In the SIEM market, meanwhile, a major shakeup sparked by Cisco’s $28 billion acquisition of Splunk has led to a series of other consolidation moves, including the merger of Exabeam and LogRhythm along with Palo Alto Networks’ $500 million acquisition of IBM’s QRadar SaaS business. Gartner’s 2024 Magic Quadrant for SIEM saw Microsoft, Splunk, IBM, Securonix and Exabeam ranked in the “leaders” quadrant. Elsewhere in the security operations platforms space, Arctic Wolf recently completed its $160 million acquisition of Cylance from BlackBerry. In the realm of threat intelligence, key providers include Google Cloud and Dataminr, while major players in risk management include Qualys, Tenable and Rapid7. What follows are the 20 security operations, risk and threat intelligence companies that made our Security 100 for 2025 . Arctic Wolf Nick Schneider President, CEO Arctic Wolf has enhanced its Aurora security oper­ations platform with the integration of SOAR tech­nology and plans to expand its capabilities further with the planned acquisition of Cylance’s endpoint security technology from BlackBerry. Meanwhile, it debuted a new module for Aurora that provides real-time threat intelligence and reporting. Axonius Dean Sysman Co-Founder, CEO Axonius expanded its offerings in cybersecurity asset management and SaaS security pos­ture management with the introduction of the Axonius Software Man­agement Module for tracking and managing all installed software. It also debuted enhancements for enabling better over­sight of SaaS usage. BlueVoyant Jim Rosenthal Co-Founder, CEO BlueVoyant unveiled its new Cyber Defense Program, integrating a number of defensive security tools— including internal, external and supply chain protec­tion—into a centralized platform. Key capabilities include managed XDR, supply chain defense, dig­ital risk protection, cyber posture management and proactive defense. Cribl Clint Sharp Co-Founder, CEO Data plat­form provider Cribl unveiled product updates including the debut of a managed data lake focused on long-term data retention, Cribl Lake. The company also unveiled AI-powered assistant Cribl Copilot and launched new and enhanced integrations for Cribl Stream including with Wiz, Oracle, Google Security Operations and OpenTelemetry. Cynomi David Primor CEO Cynomi offers an automated vCISO plat­form tailored to the needs of MSPs. The platform aims to offer equivalent capabilities to a governance, risk and compliance tool while also going further by conduct­ing gap analysis, creating customized policies and developing a prioritized remediation plan to ensure that cybersecurity is addressed as well. Dataminr Ted Bailey Founder, CEO Major launches for Dataminr included the debut of its new generative AI capability, ReGenAI. The technology provides automatic regeneration of textual descriptions throughout the unfolding of events, accelerating the delivery of up-to-date situ­ational understanding for threat teams. Devo Technology Walter Scott CEO Devo debuted its security data analyt­ics platform, including with new data orchestration capabilities focused on enhanced filter­ing and routing of data to cloud and data platforms. Other updates included the launch of the Devo Data Analytics Cloud for orchestration and ingestion of data from any source. Exabeam Chris O’Malley President, CEO Exabeam and Log­Rhythm announced the closure of their merger, with the combined company now known as Exabeam. It offers a cloud-native secu­rity operations platform as well as an on-premises SIEM platform. Recent updates included launch­ing compatibility with the OpenAPI standard for improved interoperability. Google Cloud Thomas Kurian CEO The cloud giant's new Google Threat Intelligence offering is integrated into the Google Security Operations platform. Google Threat Intelligence combines insight from three massive data sources—Mandiant, VirusTotal and Google— with new GenAI-powered capabilities. IBM Security Arvind Krishna Chairman, President, CEO The sale of its QRadar SaaS business to Palo Alto Networks comes as IBM shifts its cybersecurity strategy to focus on data security, as exemplified by its deal to acquire HashiCorp. The planned acquisition aims to bring capabilities such as data protection and identity-based security with products including HashiCorp Vault. Infima Joel Cahill Co-Founder, CEO Infima, an MSP-focused provider of highly automated security awareness train­ing, offers rapid setup and requires minimal oversight of its platform. The com­pany recently updated its platform with a simplified training invite process, newly available access to historical reports and user risk scoring. KnowBe4 Stu Sjouwerman Founder, CEO KnowBe4 , a provider of security awareness training as well as anti-phishing capabilities, expanded into offering email security with the acquisition of Egress. The KnowBe4 Cloud Email Security offering provides adaptive, AI-powered defense capabilities and email threat prevention and encryption functionality. Broadcom.description: PrivacyCookie Notice and Policy Cookie Notice and Policy Effective Date: April 15, 2026 Broadcom uses cookies and similar technologies on its website and online services (collectively, “Site” or “Sites”) so that Broadcom can improve your experience, e.g. by recognizing you whenever you visit Broadcom’s Site, providing you personalized information, remembering your marketing and product preferences, and helping you obtain the right information. In this notice, Broadcom provides more information about cookies and similar technologies, how Broadcom uses them, and how you can control Broadcom’s use of them. Broadcom’s processing of your personal data, including any personal data it collects through the use of cookies or similar technologies, is described in its Privacy Notice. Your use of Broadcom’s Site is subject to Broadcom’s Terms of Use. Additional terms may apply to online services. Cookies. Cookies are alphanumeric identifiers that are transferred to your device’s hard drive through your web browser for record-keeping purposes. Some cookies allow Broadcom to make it easier for you to navigate Broadcom’s Site, while others are used to enable a faster log-in process or to allow Broadcom to track your activities on the Site. Cookies on the Site may be first-party (set by Broadcom’s Site) or third-party (set by another website). There are two types of cookies: session and persistent cookies. Session Cookies. Session cookies exist only during a single online session. They disappear from your device when you close your browser or turn off your device. Broadcom uses session cookies to allow Broadcom’s systems to uniquely identify you during a session or while you are logged into the Site. This allows Broadcom to process your online transactions and requests and verify your identity, after you have logged in, as you move through the Site. Persistent Cookies. Persistent cookies remain on your device after you have closed your browser or turned off your device. Persistent cookies are used to recognize your device whenever you visit Broadcom's Sites and to track aggregate and statistical information about Broadcom’s users’ activity. Clear GIFs, pixel tags and other technologies. Clear GIFS (a.k.a. web beacons, web bugs or pixel tags) are tiny graphics with a unique identifier, similar in function to cookies. In contrast to cookies, which are stored on your device’s hard drive, clear GIFs are embedded invisibly on web pages. Broadcom may use clear GIFs in connection with Broadcom’s Site to, among other things, track the activities of Site visitors, help Broadcom manage content, and compile statistics about Site usage. Broadcom and Broadcom’s third-party service providers also use clear GIFs in emails to customers, to help Broadcom measure email response rates, identify when emails are viewed, and determine whether emails are forwarded. Third Party Services. Broadcom uses third-party applications to evaluate usage of Broadcom’s Site and to help improve the Site's performance and user experiences. These applications may use cookies and other tracking technologies to provide their services to Broadcom. What Cookies Are Used on Broadcom Sites? Broadcom has categorized cookie use below. Note that some cookies are set and controlled by third parties. Essential Cookies Strictly Necessary Cookies. These cookies, referred to as 'strictly necessary', 'essential' or 'required' are necessary for the website to function and cannot be disabled. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you, which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the Site will then not work. Non-Essential Cookies Performance Cookies. These cookies allow Broadcom to count visits and traffic sources so Broadcom can measure and improve the performance of the Site. They help Broadcom to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the Site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies Broadcom will not be able to monitor the Site’s performance. Functional Cookies. These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalization. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies, then some or all of these services may not function properly. Targeting Cookies. These cookies may be set through Broadcom’s Site by Broadcom’s advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not directly store personal data such as an email address, but uniquely identify your browser and device. If you do not allow these cookies, any targeted advertising directed to you will not be based on your visit to Broadcom’s Site. Social Media Cookies. These cookies are set by a range of social media services Broadcom has added to the Site to enable you to share Broadcom’s content with your networks. They are capable of tracking your browser across other sites and building up a profile of your interests. This may impact the content and messages you see on other websites you visit. If you do not allow these cookies you may not be able to use or see these sharing tools. For visitors in California, all non-essential cookies may be grouped under the label "Sell or Share My Personal Information." How Are Third-Party Ad Networks Used? Broadcom uses third parties such as network advertisers to display advertisements on Broadcom’s Sites, to assist Broadcom in displaying advertisements on third-party websites, and to evaluate the success of Broadcom’s advertising campaigns. Traditional security tools are not built to detect or stop these external risks. BrandShield’s cybersecurity solution identifies and removes threats before they impact your organization. Book A Demo External Threats Organizations Face Phishing & Security Threats Phishing sites, fake login pages, smishing campaigns, and social engineering attacks target customers, employees, and partners outside your security perimeter. BrandShield detects, prioritizes, and removes these threats before they lead to credential theft, fraud, or brand damage. Malicious Domains and Typosquatting Lookalike domains, typosquats, and cloned websites are used to impersonate trusted brands and launch phishing campaigns. BrandShield identifies malicious domain activity early and supports fast enforcement across registrars, hosts, and platforms. Executive & Brand Impersonation Threat actors impersonate executives, employees, and brand accounts to run scams, spread fraudulent content, and manipulate customers or internal teams. BrandShield detects fake profiles and coordinated impersonation networks, then helps remove them quickly. Dark Web Threats Exposed credentials, stolen data, and brand-related criminal activity often appear on dark web forums before they escalate. BrandShield monitors these hidden sources to surface relevant threats early, helping teams respond before risk spreads. AI Response Risk AI platforms surface content that may include infringing domains, misleading sources, or unauthorized sellers, influencing customer decisions before they reach traditional channels. BrandShield.title: Domain Protection
BrandShield.description: Skip to content Domain Protection for Malicious and Lookalike Domains Continuously detect, monitor, and take down malicious domains, lookalike websites, typosquatting, and cybersquatting before they are used for phishing, impersonation, fraud, or brand abuse. Book a Demo Trusted by the world’s leading companies Website Domain Protection BrandShield provides Online Domain Protection that detects and removes the infringing domains used to exploit your brand online. Our platform continuously monitors new domain registrations, DNS records, and certificates across every TLD to surface lookalike, typosquatted, and cybersquatted domains that misuse your brand name and trademarks. Left unchecked, these domains divert customers to competitors, host fake stores and counterfeit goods, and damage the reputation you’ve invested years in building. BrandShield gives your brand, legal, and marketing teams full visibility into how your name is being abused across the web. Once an infringing domain is detected, our expert enforcement team drives fast takedowns at the registrar, registry, and hosting level, and handles trademark escalation when needed. Brands move from chasing abuse reactively to protecting their name proactively, at scale. Book a Demo Take Down Fake Domains Before They Turn into Lost Revenue Malicious domains do not always become dangerous immediately after registration. Threat actors may register domains weeks or months before using them for phishing campaigns, fake websites, counterfeit sales, or executive impersonation. BrandShield monitors newly registered and existing domains for variations of your brand and other protected assets. Suspicious registrations are continuously assessed so threats can be identified before customers or employees encounter them. Book a Demo The Growing Risk of Malicious Domains 1.5M+ Domain names were used in phishing attacks during the 12 months analyzed by Interisle’s 2025 Phishing Landscape study. 77% Of domain names used for phishing were maliciously registered by cybercriminals rather than compromised legitimate domains. 10–20% Of newly registered gTLD domains in 2025 may have been purchased by malicious actors, according to Interisle research. Full-Spectrum Domain Protection Solution AI-Powered Domain Detection Continuously scan domain registrations for brand names, product names, executive identities, trademarks, common misspellings, homoglyphs, and suspicious keyword combinations. Typosquatting Detection Detect domains designed around common typing errors, missing characters, added characters, alternative spellings, and visually similar variations of your legitimate domain. Enforcement Experts Experienced and knowledgeable enforcement managers analyze your company threats to determine efficient course of action. Lookalike Domain Monitoring Detect malicious domains, hosting infrastructure, and spoofed websites as they are created. Enforcement & Takedowns BrandShield combines automated detection with experienced enforcement specialists who investigate confirmed threats and determine the appropriate remediation path. Centralized Reporting Periodic and other detailed reports with monitoring, detection and enforcement activities. Augury.title: R&D AI-Native Mobile Engineer – Deployment Platform Haifa, Israel (Hybrid)
Augury.description: AI-Native Mobile Engineer - Deployment Platform | Augury About The Position You will join the Deployment Platform team, which puts Augury's technology directly in the hands of customers, field technicians, and partners. As an AI-Native mobile engineer, your primary development framework is Flutter (with native iOS and Android used when needed), building the mobile application central to Augury's field deployment. You are also comfortable across the full stack to ensure end-to-end feature delivery. Most importantly, you will shape the next generation of agentic installation experiences that define how industrial AI reaches the factory floor. This is a high-impact role at the intersection of mobile, IoT, and AI. A Day In Your Life Design, build, and maintain high-quality, cross-platform mobile applications for iOS and Android using the core Flutter/Dart stack. Lead the design and shipment of agentic-first workflows for guided installation, leveraging LLMs (Azure OpenAI, Gemini) to assist technicians and automate decision-making in the field. Implement complex IoT/Hardware integration features, including NFC provisioning, AR field tools, and indoor positioning/navigation. Contribute to backend and frontend services/APIs to ensure seamless, end-to-end feature delivery. Architect and maintain a scalable, modular monorepo, ensuring robustness through strong state management (BLoC/RxDart) and comprehensive test coverage. Collaborate with product and design teams to deliver exceptional UI/UX, including adaptive and RTL-aware layouts. What You Bring Agentic-First Mindset & Proven Experience as an AI-Native Engineer utilizing tools like Claude, Cursor, or Gemini to enhance productivity and quality in commercial development. 5+ years of mobile development experience with proficiency in Flutter/Dart and native iOS/Android, BLoC state management, and designing scalable mobile architecture. Comfortable with full-stack contributions to backend and frontend services/APIs to ensure end-to-end feature ownership. Proven ability to write high-quality, testable Dart code with cross-platform (iOS/Android) and RTL familiarity. Strong Advantage Experience with industrial IoT and field-service applications, including device commissioning workflows, hands-on IoT connectivity (Wi-Fi, NFC, BLE, and Beacons APIs), and familiarity with AR and Indoor Navigation. Familiarity with Firebase, third-party support tooling (Intercom), and Offline/Sync capabilities. Tech Stack Flutter, Dart, Modular Monorepos, BLoC, RxDart, Go_router, Python, Go, Azure OpenAI, Gemini, MongoDB Atlas, REST APIs, Microservices, NFC, BLE, Beacons, and WiFi. What Success Looks Like Build reusable, high-quality mobile components and architecture. Ship reliable, production-ready mobile features and enhance the user experience. Utilize the AI Native Development process in your day-to-day to improve workflows and the product. Contribute to the overall product infrastructure and backend services when mobile expertise is needed. Improve the mobile application's performance, stability, and maintainability (e.g., state management, threading, data synchronization). Contribute to practical standards around mobile architecture, testing, monitoring, security, and deployment (CI/CD).
